interactions.label: A woman's LMP is recorded wrongly, so her gestation is charted as 30 weeks when

params.question: A woman's LMP is recorded wrongly, so her gestation is charted as 30 weeks when she is actually 34 weeks. Which management decision is most directly compromised?

answers.text: Timing of antenatal corticosteroids for fetal lung maturity, and preterm delivery planning

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Gestational age is the reference point for steroid timing and preterm management, so a four-week dating error shifts both decisions.

answers.text: Measurement of the pelvic inlet on clinical examination

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Pelvic inlet dimensions are a fixed anatomical measurement taken on examination. They do not depend on the gestational age recorded in the history.

answers.text: Dosing of iron and folic acid tablets

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The IFA dose is standard and does not vary with gestation, so a dating error does not change it.

answers.text: Screening for thalassaemia carrier status from the family history

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Carrier screening depends on family and ethnic history, not on the gestational age recorded from the LMP.

overallFeedback.feedback: The LMP sets gestational age, and gestational age drives steroid timing and preterm delivery planning. A four-week dating error can change those decisions.
Gestational age is the reference point for nearly every antenatal decision, which is why the LMP in the obstetric history must be recorded correctly.

params.question: A woman with no previous pregnancy problems plans to conceive next month. When should folic acid supplementation start to reduce the risk of neural tube defects?

answers.text: Three months before conception, continuing through the first trimester

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. The neural tube closes in the first weeks of pregnancy, often before a woman knows she is pregnant, so supplementation must start before conception.

answers.text: Only after the first trimester, once the neural tube has closed

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The neural tube closes within the first few weeks after conception, so starting after the first trimester is too late to prevent the defect.

answers.text: From the 20th week, when placental transfer of folate increases

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Protection against neural tube defects depends on folate status at the time of neural tube closure, which is much earlier than 20 weeks.

answers.text: Only in women with a previous pregnancy affected by a neural tube defect

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Neural tube defect prevention is a universal recommendation, because most affected pregnancies occur in women with no prior history.

overallFeedback.feedback: Neural tube closure happens within the first weeks after conception. Folic acid must therefore start three months before conception and continue through the first trimester.
Folic acid taken before conception and through the first trimester covers the period of neural tube closure, which is why this counselling applies to every woman planning pregnancy.

interactions.label: A biophysical profile score of 4 out of 10 is found at 36 weeks in a primary hea

params.question: A biophysical profile score of 4 out of 10 is found at 36 weeks in a primary health centre with no neonatal intensive care unit. What is the most appropriate response?

answers.text: Urgent transfer to a facility with neonatal intensive care, weighing transport time against the risk

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. A score of 4 at 36 weeks indicates real compromise, and the response should match the facility's ability to care for a newborn, so urgent transfer is the right step.

answers.text: Immediate delivery at the primary health centre

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Delivering without neonatal intensive care exposes a possibly compromised newborn to risk that the facility cannot manage. The facility's resources must shape the decision.

answers.text: Repeat the profile after two weeks at home

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: A score of 4 at 36 weeks is concerning, and a two-week delay risks intrauterine death in a compromised fetus.

answers.text: Discharge with routine follow-up, since the score is above the midpoint

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: A score of 4 out of 10 is abnormal and is not a reassuring result, so routine follow-up would under-react to the finding.

overallFeedback.feedback: A biophysical profile of 4 at 36 weeks signals real compromise. The response should weigh gestation and facility resources, which here points to urgent transfer to neonatal care.
Surveillance findings are graded, not binary. The same score calls for different action depending on gestation and what the facility can offer a newborn.

interactions.label: A stillborn baby shows skin slippage and overlapping skull bones on examination.

params.question: A stillborn baby shows skin slippage and overlapping skull bones on examination. What does this finding indicate?

answers.text: A macerated stillbirth, with death well before the onset of labour

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Maceration takes time to develop, so skin slippage and overlapping skull bones (Spalding's sign) indicate that the fetus died well before labour began.

answers.text: A fresh stillbirth, with death within the last day during labour

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: A fresh stillbirth has intact skin and preserved structure, because maceration has not yet developed in the short time since death.

answers.text: An early neonatal death after a live birth

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: A neonatal death follows a live birth, whereas a stillbirth has no signs of life at delivery, so maceration does not classify the event as a neonatal death.

answers.text: A loss before 20 weeks, classified as an abortion

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: A loss before 20 weeks is classified as an abortion. Maceration is used to classify stillbirths, and the signs described here do not define an abortion.

overallFeedback.feedback: Skin slippage and overlapping skull bones (Spalding's sign) indicate maceration, which means death occurred well before labour began.
Maceration reflects how long the fetus has been dead. A macerated stillbirth points to death well before labour, and ultrasound confirms the diagnosis before it is shared with the family.

interactions.label: Priya's severe pre-eclampsia developed silently over several weeks. Which routin

params.question: Priya's severe pre-eclampsia developed silently over several weeks. Which routine ANC practice, applied at every visit, would most likely have flagged it earliest?

answers.text: Serial blood pressure and urine protein measurement at every visit

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Rising blood pressure and proteinuria are the earliest markers of pre-eclampsia, and both are picked up only through regular measurement at each contact.

answers.text: A single haemoglobin check at booking

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: A haemoglobin check gives information about anaemia, but it does not detect the blood pressure rise or proteinuria that mark pre-eclampsia.

answers.text: Oral glucose tolerance test at 24 to 28 weeks

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The glucose tolerance test screens for gestational diabetes, which is a different condition with a different mechanism from pre-eclampsia.

answers.text: Fetal anomaly ultrasound in the third trimester only

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Anomaly ultrasound looks for structural fetal abnormalities. It does not detect the maternal blood pressure and proteinuria changes of pre-eclampsia.

overallFeedback.feedback: Pre-eclampsia shows up first as rising blood pressure and proteinuria. Only regular measurement at every ANC visit reliably catches these changes early.
Regular blood pressure and urine protein checks at each visit are the core of pre-eclampsia surveillance, and missing them lets the disease progress silently.
